notes: §1985:IX.2.7.3 SR2: "Data-name-1 must reference a data item of the category alphanumeric within a record description entry associated with the file-name to which the RECORD KEY clause is subordinate." FileControlBinder.ResolveFiles screens every file control entry through FileControlKeyRules.Screen, whose table (Rules) holds two PrimeRecordKey rows for the rule: the location row refuses a key that names nothing or an item whose level-01 record is not one of the file's (RecordLayout.IsInRecordOfFile), and the category row refuses an item that ItemCategory.IsAlphanumericOrNational does not admit, both as error COBOL0863. The table has no edition column and 1985 needs none: the one category 2023 adds, national, cannot be declared at --std 85 (COBOL0900), and the SOURCE-phrase row has no 1985 syntax to reach it. A group item is admitted as alphanumeric, which the 1985 clause itself supposes (§1985:IX.2.7.3 SR3 speaks of data-name-1 referencing a group item). The witness is refused for a PIC 9(5) prime key. Probed further at --std 85: alphabetic, alphanumeric-edited, numeric-edited, COMP and numeric prime keys, a key in WORKING-STORAGE, a key in another file's record, an undefined name and a condition-name each draw COBOL0863; a group key holding numeric items, a qualified PIC X key in the file's second record and the level-01 record itself are accepted.

next.reason: 1985: "Data-name-1 must reference a data item of the category alphanumeric"; 2023: "shall reference a data item of category alphanumeric or category national". Both require the key to lie in a record of the associated file. 2023 also accepts a category national key (and data-name-2), which 1985 refused.
